findings.why_it_matters: Every Retract, Correct, and CorrectInterval dispatches to `retract_derived`, which walks the complete runtime event log to find Behavior rows whose `caused_by` equals the target event. findings.title: Probe Horn premises through relation-keyed candidates
findings.why_it_matters: For every remaining Horn premise, `search_at` calls `live_facts_at`, which materializes a vector after walking every `vt_by_from` bucket at or before the valid-time cut, and recursive candidates repeat that full scan. A two-premise rule can therefore rescan and allocate the N-fact live set for each candidate from the first premise, making normal rule firing quadratic in graph size; longer rules compound the walk. Iterate a relation-keyed live-fact index and choose the next bound premise without rebuilding the global live set.

findings.title: Build incremental appends from the undisclosed suffix only
findings.why_it_matters: Every `Persister::append` calls `collect_new`, which first calls `encoded_log`; that helper clones every dictionary string and every graph event accumulated so far. `collect_new` then moves the full encoding into another graph vector and clones only the suffix into a third vector. Appending one new event to an N-event runtime therefore costs O(N) CPU and temporary memory, and a stream of small appends becomes O(N²). residual_risks.detail: Both builders allocate the temporary `Vec<&Fact>` returned by `live_facts_at` before building CSR buckets. This is measurable at large N, but the visible materializer path is an explicit one-time lease build, so it does not clear the persona threshold without evidence of repeated production rebuilds.

The fallback scans all fold facts, but `bind_reserved` rebuilds the `horns_by_premise` lease and marks it ready; the normal ingest path therefore uses the keyed lease. No production-observable hot fallback was established.

The exact ValidTime/WallTime facade parameters are a source break for callers passing bare u64 or the wrong clock. All visible in-repo consumers are migrated and compile-fail tests deliberately pin the narrowing.

For identifier-like rule names the public digest changes from domain+UTF-8 to domain+canonical RuleAst bytes. Visible callers recompute the pin rather than hard-code it, but out-of-repo cached pins require explicit migration/versioning.
The envelope and all five variants are new; the visible example dispatches Ok, Conflict, Abstain, Unknown, and MissingAnchor exhaustively. No pre-existing consumer is broken by the addition.
The JSONL-to-triple mapper is unchanged in this patch; the binary only wraps the query cutoff in ValidTime, so the consumed H2 row shape is unchanged.

residual_risks: Removed pre-Phase-26 Op variants are an explicitly documented open/migration break in docs/process/op-compat.md and m050_op_compat, not a silent defect; a real migration remains deferred work.

Legacy Behavior rows without rule_version deserialize but fail the new strict replay gate; this is adjacent to the documented strict-replay policy and needs an explicit vintage decision rather than a silent alias.
The write lock is process-local flock-based; cross-process or cross-host writers outside this API still need an external coordinator.
Horn search still binds MAX_VAR=16 and explores live facts at one point; richer rules need explicit limits and complete-window semantics before production rule execution.
Governor selftest derives mutations only from configured step shapes; presence/correspondence invariants that are not representable as mutations remain proven only by review.
Parallel worker fallback preserves check results but can duplicate side effects on submission failure until the pool contract is made at-most-once.
